_comment: Feeling Scale (FS) catalog onboarding. Source: Hardy, C. J., & Rejeski, W. J. (1989). Not what, but how one feels: The measurement of affect during exercise. Journal of Sport & Exercise Psychology, 11(3), 304-317, plus secondary validation/review literature (e.g. PMC10653427 systematic review on FS/FAS use in resistance training; ACSM guidance citing FS for monitoring affective valence during exercise). Single-item, 11-point bipolar scale from -5 (Very bad) to +5 (Very good), 0 = Neutral; only odd integers and 0 are verbally anchored, even non-zero integers (-4,-2,2,4) are numeric-only. Standard administration prompt: 'How do you feel right now?'. Reuses the existing 'Subjective Exercise Experience' phenomenon already in the catalog (added for SEES) rather than creating a near-duplicate, since FS measures a momentary affective response to exercise that falls within that same phenomenon.

study.title: Feeling Scale (FS) - Instrument Onboarding
study.objective: Register the Feeling Scale (FS) instrument and its single affective-valence dimension into the GDX_HUMAN psychometric catalog as reusable knowledge for future exercise-psychology studies.
study.method: Desk research of the published instrument (Hardy & Rejeski, 1989) and secondary validation/review literature; catalog registration only, no primary data collection associated with this record.

instruments.name: Feeling Scale (FS)
instruments.description: Hardy, C. J., & Rejeski, W. J. (1989). Not what, but how one feels: The measurement of affect during exercise. Journal of Sport & Exercise Psychology, 11(3), 304-317.
instruments.instructions: Respond to the single question below by circling the number that best describes how you feel right now, at this moment. There are no right or wrong answers; respond as honestly and spontaneously as possible. This item is typically repeated at regular intervals during and/or immediately after exercise.
instruments.phenomenon_description: The pattern of affective and psychological responses -- positive well-being, psychological distress, and fatigue -- that individuals report during or immediately after a bout of physical exercise.

constructs.name: Affective Valence (Feeling Scale)
constructs.definition: Core affective valence (pleasure versus displeasure) experienced by an individual at a given moment during or immediately after physical exercise, per the circumplex model of affect.

variables.name: Affective Valence (FS)
variables.description: Momentary self-reported feeling of pleasure versus displeasure in response to exercise.
variables.operational_definition: Single-item response to 'How do you feel right now?' on an 11-point bipolar scale from -5 (Very bad) to +5 (Very good), 0 = Neutral.
variables.indicator_description: Raw score of the single Feeling Scale item, from -5 to +5.

items.statement_text: How do you feel right now?
